fullDescription: A landing page UI for an independent long-form interview podcast, built on one idea: time is the page's only constant. Every episode is a bar whose width is its real runtime at a single shared scale of 1 minute = 6 px, so a 2:11:00 conversation is literally twice the length of a 1:01:00 one and you read the archive without reading a number. The newest episode gets a full-scale bar with chapter markers at their true timestamps and a loud hatched lane over the 32 minutes the host has not indexed yet. Season totals are the same episodes laid end to end and wrapped like a line of text, at the same constant, so there is no second scale anywhere. Flat saturated pale-cyan ground, heavy near-black and deep-indigo blocks, hot-pink ticks, one yellow annotation. Reusable for any page where rows carry a comparable duration or quantity.

structured.summary: A LANDING / MARKETING SITE for one independent long-form interview podcast, whose entire point of view is that TIME IS THE PAGE'S SINGLE CONSTANT. Set one CSS custom property `--ppm: 6px` (pixels per minute) and derive EVERY drawn length on the page from it with calc() so nothing is a hand-tuned width. The page opens with no hero banner and no headline describing the idea: top-left a compact masthead (show name in a heavy geometric display face across two lines in indigo #4242fa, one line of what the show is, a plain-text row of subscribe destinations), and immediately beside it THREE MOST RECENT EPISODES ALREADY PLOTTED, each as episode number + title above a solid near-black #0a0c10 bar at calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes) with the runtime in mono at the bar's end, over a SCALE KEY RULER ticked every 15 minutes with mono labels. Then: (2) LATEST EPISODE AT FULL SCALE, one deep-indigo #2c0b8e bar spanning the content width with hot-pink #e60067 chapter ticks at their real timestamp offsets, chapter labels stepped beneath in two alternating rows, a hatched hot-pink lane over the stretch with no chapter index drawn LOUDER than any solid bar, a small yellow #ffd43b annotation sitting ON the dark bar pointing at the hatch, and a black PLAY control with the runtime on it. (3) EVERY EPISODE TO SCALE, the full archive of 14 rows across 2 seasons on the same constant, each row number + title + guest + date + bar + runtime, with only a hairline #dceff9 baseline tick as the track and never a filled slab behind the bar. (4) SEASON TOTALS AS A REAL RATIO, each season's episodes laid END TO END at the same --ppm and WRAPPED across full-width rows like a line of text, with a pink tick where one episode ends and the next starts, so one season visibly occupies nearly twice the folded block of the other. (5) an ABOUT panel on a flat pale #eaf6fc block, paragraph left and a mono production-facts column right (RECORDED, CUTS, CHAPTER INDEX, CADENCE, LONGEST, SHORTEST). (6) SUBSCRIBE, a plain text link row plus an email field. Flat saturated pale-cyan #cbe9f7 ground throughout, no gradients, no shadows, no textures, no photography. Fully responsive: on smaller widths override the single --ppm to a smaller INTEGER so the constant still holds and every bar stays to scale.

style.description: Colour-block information design on a saturated pale-cyan field. Flat #cbe9f7 ground with zero gradients, glass, blur, drop-shadows, textures or paper metaphor, so the only things with weight on the page are the DRAWN MARKS: heavy near-black #0a0c10 and deep-indigo #2c0b8e blocks with hard edges. Colour is strictly role-bound: near-black for archive bars and body type, deep indigo for the featured bar and section headings, hot pink #e60067 for eyebrow labels, chapter ticks and the hatch, indigo #4242fa for the wordmark and links, and yellow #ffd43b confined to a single annotation sitting on top of a dark bar (it has no contrast against the cyan ground and must never touch it). Type is a heavy geometric display face set large and tight for the show name and section heads, a neutral grotesque for prose, and a monospace for every number: timestamps, runtimes, ruler labels, production facts. The aesthetic is deliberately austere and chart-like, and the distinctiveness is structural rather than stylistic: swap the palette and the design survives, because the design IS the scale system.
style.prompt: Design on a FLAT saturated pale-cyan #cbe9f7 ground with no gradient, glass, blur, shadow, texture or paper metaphor anywhere. Give weight only to the drawn marks: hard-edged near-black #0a0c10 and deep-indigo #2c0b8e blocks. Bind colour to roles and do not deviate: near-black archive bars and body text, deep indigo for the featured bar and section headings, hot pink #e60067 for small uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow labels, chapter ticks and the hatch pattern, indigo #4242fa for the wordmark and links, pale #eaf6fc for one panel and for type reversed out of black, hairline #dceff9 for baselines, and yellow #ffd43b ONLY as an annotation sitting on top of a dark bar (never on the cyan ground, where it has no contrast). Use a heavy geometric display face (Funnel Display 700) large and tight for the show name and section heads, a neutral grotesque (Inter Tight) for prose, and a monospace (DM Mono) for EVERY number. Do NOT add a faint dot-grid or line-grid background, a centered headline over a glow band, decorative status pills, a symmetrical three-up trust strip, a device-showcase strip, cover art, portraits, avatars, logos or any photograph. No em-dashes in visible copy, no emoji, no lorem, no invented statistics.

layout_and_structure.description: A scrolling six-section landing page that opens ON its own mechanic rather than announcing it. (1) Masthead beside three recent episodes already plotted, over a scale-key ruler. (2) The latest episode at full scale with chapter ticks and a hatched unindexed lane. (3) The whole archive to scale, grouped by season. (4) Season totals as folded strips at the same constant. (5) An about panel with a mono production-facts column. (6) Subscribe. Uniform vertical rhythm between sections, one content width, everything left-aligned to a single origin so bar lengths are directly comparable down the page. Reflows to one column on mobile with the scale constant reduced to a smaller integer rather than abandoned.

prompts.part: Masthead plus the three plotted recent episodes and the scale key
prompts.partPt: Masthead plus the three plotted recent episodes and the scale key
prompts.prompt: Build the top of the page as a two-column split with NO hero banner and NO headline describing the idea. Left: the show name in a heavy geometric display face broken across two lines in indigo #4242fa, one plain sentence of what the show is and who hosts it, and a row of small monospace subscribe links (RSS, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube). Right: a small hot-pink uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow reading THREE MOST RECENT EPISODES, PLOTTED AT THEIR REAL RUNTIME, then three rows, each with the episode number and title on one line and beneath it a solid near-black #0a0c10 bar about 22px tall whose width is calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes), with the runtime in monospace immediately after the bar's right end. All three bars start at the same left origin so their different lengths are the point. Below them a second pink eyebrow stating the constant (SCALE KEY. 1 MINUTE = 6 PX. EVERY BAR ON THIS PAGE IS DRAWN AT IT.) and a RULER: a hairline axis with ticks at 0/15/30/45/60/75/90/105/120 minutes, positioned with the same calc(), monospace labels beneath, and the word MINUTES under the origin.

A section headed LATEST EPISODE, AT FULL SCALE in deep indigo #2c0b8e. Beneath it a monospace meta line (EPISODE 14 · 14 JULY 2026 · 2:08:00), the episode title very large in the display face, and the guest name. Then ONE deep-indigo #2c0b8e bar about 50px tall at calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes), carrying: hot-pink #e60067 vertical chapter ticks at calc(var(--ppm) * timestamp_minutes) from the bar's own left edge; a hot-pink HATCHED lane (repeating-linear-gradient 45deg) filling the stretch from where the chapter index stops to the end of the bar, drawn louder and higher-contrast than any solid bar on the page; and a small yellow #ffd43b annotation block with dark text reading NO INDEX HERE YET sitting INSIDE the dark bar next to the hatch, layered above the ticks. The runtime sits in the display face just past the bar's end. Below the bar, chapter labels stepped in two alternating rows so they never collide: pink monospace timestamp over a small uppercase chapter title, each left-aligned to its tick, plus a final pink note at the hatch reading the index stop time and how many minutes are unmarked. Then a black play control (a triangle glyph plus PLAY and the runtime in monospace, pale #eaf6fc text) beside a one-sentence plain description of the conversation.

A section headed EVERY EPISODE, TO SCALE with one line of prose stating that all episodes share the same constant and you can see it without reading a number. Group the rows under small hot-pink season eyebrows (SEASON 2, 2026 / SEASON 1, 2025), newest first. Each row: a monospace episode number, the title in small bold uppercase, the guest name, and the date, on one line above a solid near-black #0a0c10 bar at calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes) with the runtime in monospace after its right end. The bar's track must be ONLY a hairline #dceff9 baseline rule the full content width, never a filled slab behind the bar, so the mark always out-inks its container. Do not truncate titles. Close the section with a repeat of the same ruler and the note SAME SCALE KEY. 1 MINUTE = 6 PX.

A section headed SEASON TOTALS, AS A REAL RATIO, with one line of prose explaining the device and NOT excusing any exception to the constant: every episode laid end to end at the same 1 minute = 6 px, wrapped to the page like a line of text, ticks where one episode ends and the next starts. For each season: a monospace label with its episode count, the total duration in the display face (15 h 8 m), then a WRAPPING container of per-episode segments each at calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes), so the strip folds onto multiple full-width rows and the last row is a short stub. Mark each episode boundary with an inset hot-pink box-shadow on the segment's trailing edge so the tick adds no layout width. Use deep indigo for one season's strip and near-black for the other. The longer season must visibly occupy nearly twice the folded block of the shorter one. Under both, a single display-face line stating the episode count and the total hours of tape. There must be NO second scale and no sentence anywhere on the page explaining a scale exception.

ABOUT THE SHOW as a flat pale #eaf6fc panel with a hairline #dceff9 border, no shadow, filling the full content width as a two-column split: left a short paragraph in the body face explaining how the show is made and why the site draws episodes at their real lengths; right a narrow definition-list column of production facts, each a small hot-pink uppercase label over a monospace value (RECORDED / CUTS / CHAPTER INDEX / CADENCE / LONGEST / SHORTEST), where LONGEST and SHORTEST carry the real extreme runtimes and their episode numbers and titles and must agree exactly with the bars above. Stacks to one column on mobile. Then a SUBSCRIBE section: a plain monospace text row of platform destinations on the left and an email field with a black submit button on the right, no logo marquee and no testimonials. Close with a hairline rule, the wordmark, and a monospace copyright line.

special_ui_components.component: One shared scale constant every length derives from
special_ui_components.description: The whole design is a single CSS custom property. Nothing on the page is a hand-tuned width, which is what makes the claim checkable.
special_ui_components.prompt: Declare one custom property `--ppm: 6px` (pixels per minute) on the root and derive EVERY drawn length on the page from it with calc(): bar widths as calc(var(--ppm) * runtime_minutes), chapter tick offsets as calc(var(--ppm) * timestamp_minutes), ruler tick positions the same way. Never type a pixel width for a mark. Print the constant on screen as a scale key. At each breakpoint override ONLY `--ppm`, and only to an INTEGER value (6 / 4 / 3 / 2) so sub-pixel layout rounding cannot introduce a per-element exception, and make the on-screen scale-key text track the breakpoint (a ::after with content per media query) so the stated number stays true at every width. The result is that every length on the page can be measured against every other one.

special_ui_components.description: A hairline axis with ticks every 15 minutes that lets a reader measure any bar on the page.
special_ui_components.prompt: Draw a hairline axis the width of the plotted area with vertical ticks positioned at calc(var(--ppm) * N) for N at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105, 120 minutes, small monospace numerals beneath each tick, and the unit word (MINUTES) under the origin. Repeat it at the foot of the archive so the reader never has to scroll back to check the constant.

special_ui_components.component: Chapter ticks riding on a full-scale bar
special_ui_components.description: Chapter markers at their true timestamps inside the bar, with labels stepped so they never collide.
special_ui_components.prompt: Inside the featured bar, absolutely position hot-pink #e60067 vertical ticks at calc(var(--ppm) * timestamp_minutes) from the bar's own left edge. Beneath the bar, lay the chapter labels in two alternating rows (odd chapters on the first row, even on the second) each absolutely positioned to its tick, a pink monospace timestamp above a small uppercase chapter title, so dense chapters never overlap. On narrow viewports swap the absolutely-positioned labels for a plain stacked list with a display:!important toggle, since a utility-class stylesheet injected after your inline styles can otherwise leave both visible.

special_ui_components.component: Hatched no-data lane, drawn louder than the real data
special_ui_components.description: The missing chapter index is the ugliest, loudest mark on the page. It is an opinion, not a gap.
special_ui_components.prompt: Fill the stretch of the bar between where the chapter index stops and the end of the episode with a hot-pink #e60067 45-degree repeating-linear-gradient hatch, sized so it reads as texture at a glance, and give it MORE visual force than any solid bar on the page. Add a small yellow #ffd43b annotation block with dark text (NO INDEX HERE YET) sitting inside the dark bar beside the hatch, layered above the ticks so no tick slices through it, and a pink note beneath stating the index stop timestamp and how many minutes are unmarked. Reuse this for any row where a comparable quantity is genuinely missing: hiding a number should cost you your bar and earn you the ugliest mark on the page.

special_ui_components.component: Folded strip: a total drawn at the same constant by wrapping
special_ui_components.description: How to show a sum that is 5448px long without inventing a second scale.
special_ui_components.prompt: To show a total that cannot fit a viewport, do NOT introduce a reduced scale. Lay the components end to end at the page's own `--ppm` inside a WRAPPING inline container so the strip folds onto multiple full-width rows like a line of text, and let folds land mid-component, which is honest. Mark each component boundary with an inset box-shadow on the trailing edge (inset -2px 0 0 <accent>) so the tick adds zero layout width. The reader compares two folded blocks by row count and stub length, the constant is never broken, and the page needs no disclaimer.

special_ui_components.component: Bar rows whose track is a hairline, never a slab
special_ui_components.description: Keeps the mark out-inking its own container, which is what stops a board of bars squinting down into identical slabs.
special_ui_components.prompt: For each row, draw the bar as a solid block at its true width and give it only a hairline baseline rule (1px, #dceff9) running the full content width as its track. Never put a filled or tinted slab behind the bar: an empty container of the same height as the mark will out-mass the signal and the whole board reduces to identical rectangles at a distance. Left-align every bar to one origin down the page so lengths are directly comparable.

special_ui_components.component: Production-facts column derived from the data, not typed
special_ui_components.description: Extreme values printed beside the chart, guaranteed to agree with it.
special_ui_components.prompt: Beside the about paragraph, add a narrow definition list of production facts, each a small uppercase hot-pink label over a monospace value. For any fact that restates the data (LONGEST, SHORTEST, totals, counts), compute it with max/min/sum over the same source array the bars are drawn from rather than typing it, so the panel can never drift from the chart. A design that makes a checkable claim beside its own data must make the claim true.
